crm.title: CRM integration
crm.description: Send call data to your CRM after each call. Configure server URL and authentication.
crm.enableDesc: When enabled, call data will be sent to your CRM system after each call ends.
crm.loadFailed: The CRM settings could not be loaded. Saving is off so the stored settings are not overwritten.
crm.loadFailedSave: The saved settings could not be loaded, so saving is off.
crm.notActive: CRM is enabled but not active: {{reason}}. Calls are logged as failed deliveries until this is fixed.
crm.notActiveUnknown: the connection could not be built
crm.durationHint: How duration and talk time are sent. In seconds mode the keys become durationInSeconds / talkTimeInSeconds, so the receiver cannot misread the unit.
crm.keyNamesHint: Rename any field to the key your CRM expects. Leave blank to use the default.
crm.collisionWarn: Two fields would be sent under the same key ({{keys}}). The duplicate rename is dropped and the field keeps its default key.
crm.outcomeMapHint: Remap an outcome to what your CRM expects (e.g. BUSY → UNANSWERED). Applies to both status and disposition. Leave blank to send unchanged.
crm.connectionSub: Where OpDesk reaches your CRM and how it authenticates.
crm.verifySSLDesc: Turn off only for a CRM using a self-signed certificate.
crm.blockPrivateDesc: Loopback and cloud-metadata are always blocked. Enable only if your CRM is public — it rejects on-prem/LAN URLs.
crm.deliverySub: When a call ends, where the record goes and which calls qualify.
crm.syncOffNote: Call-data sync is paused — no call records are pushed. The connection above stays configured.
crm.syncEndpointHint: Appended to the server URL. Leave blank to use the connection endpoint path.
crm.triggerHint: After wrap-up waits until the agent who took the call finishes wrap-up, so the record matches the final call log. Unanswered calls go at once.
crm.wrapupTimeoutHint: Push anyway if wrap-up has not ended by then.
crm.retryDesc: A push that times out, gets a server error or is rate-limited is sent again with the same idempotency key. A push the CRM rejects (4xx) is not retried; resend it from Logs.
crm.retryDelaysHint: Comma-separated; the last value repeats. A longer Retry-After from the CRM wins.
crm.retryLogHint: Every push and each retry is listed under Logs → CRM Deliveries.
crm.noDirections: No direction selected — nothing will be pushed.
crm.payloadSub: Choose the values to send and, if needed, the key each one lands under.
crm.noCatalog: The field catalog could not be loaded. Reload the page and try again.
crm.slashWarn: The endpoint path has no leading slash — it is joined to the server URL exactly as shown above.
crm.previewPaused: Call-data sync is paused — nothing is pushed.
crm.previewEmpty: No fields selected — the CRM would receive an empty body.
crm.previewHintAll: Example values — pushed after every call.
crm.previewHintNone: Example values. No direction is selected, so nothing is pushed.
crm.previewHintSome: Example values — pushed after every {{dirs}} call.
crm.lookupSub: Resolve caller numbers to CRM contact names, shown on the softphone and dashboards. Results are cached server-side.
crm.lookupOffNote: Contact lookup is off — calls show bare numbers. The connection above stays configured.
crm.lookupUrlHint: Appended to the server URL. [Number] is replaced with the caller’s number; without it, ?phone=[Number] is added automatically.
crm.lookupNameTemplateHint: Each [path] is a dot/index path into the JSON response (data.0.name reads response.data[0].name). Multiple paths are joined, e.g. first + last name.
crm.lookupMatchDigitsHint: Caching and verification compare only the last N digits, so +20…, 0020… and 0… match the same contact. 0 = full number.
crm.lookupVerifyPathHint: Path to the phone field of the returned record. A result only counts when it matches the searched number — protects against fuzzy-search false positives.
crm.lookupTtlHint: How long a "no match" answer is remembered before the CRM is asked about that number again. Matched contacts are saved to the phonebook permanently.
crm.lookupTestNoMatch: The CRM answered, but no name was extracted. Check the name template against the response below.

contactCenter.title: Wrap-up and shift reset
contactCenter.description: After-call work and the daily logout that closes each shift.
contactCenter.wrapUpHelp: How long an agent stays paused after a queue call before returning to Ready. They can finish sooner from their status menu, so this is a ceiling, not a fixed delay. 0 turns the auto-release off. Applies from the next completed call.
contactCenter.shiftResetHelp: At this time each day every signed-in agent is logged out of their queues, so a shift left open does not run into the next one and Agent Adherence reports one shift per day. An agent on a call is logged out when the call ends; an agent on Do Not Disturb is left alone. Clear the field to turn the reset off.

internal.text: Calls between extensions. Shown for the time they take, but not customer work: they are not in the total and do not count towards the rank.

slaContribution.text: How often this agent picked up queue calls in time. Blank if they take no queue calls.
slaContribution.formula: answered in time ÷ queue calls answered

shortAbandonShare.text: Inbound callers who hung up within the short-abandon threshold — usually misdials.

recovered.text: Callers who gave up waiting in a queue and whom an agent rang back within {{hours}} hours. Counted in people: three abandons and one call back is one caller recovered.
recovered.formula: callers rung back ÷ callers who abandoned

netAbandon.text: The abandon rate with the calls of the callers we rang back taken out. The abandon rate itself still counts them.
netAbandon.formula: (abandoned − abandoned calls of recovered callers) ÷ offered

inboundOutcomes.text: Inbound calls per day: answered, and the ones nobody answered — queue abandons and missed direct calls together.

queueService.text: How the queues treated the people who waited in them: how fast they were answered, how many gave up, and whether they had to call again.

mobileWake.markerHint: Text in the SIP User-Agent that marks a mobile client, so a desk phone on the same extension does not count as the phone waking up. Contacts with RFC 8599 pn-* parameters always count.

queueAgents.text: Agents on this queue and what they're doing.

dashboard.todayUnavailable: Today's summary is not available for your role.

answerRate.text: Share of the distinct outside numbers involved that were actually spoken to — however many calls each of them took. It counts people, so ten tries to one person who finally picks up is one person reached. Internal calls between extensions are left out.

contactRate.text: Share of the calls that connected — every call counted, so a number tried five times counts five times. Answer rate counts the people behind the calls instead.

aht.text: Average handle time: the average talk time of an answered call.

totalCalls.text: Every call in this period — in, out and internal.

answered.text: Calls that actually connected and had talk time.

abandoned.text: Callers who hung up in a queue before an agent answered. A direct call to an extension that rang out is not an abandon.

abandonRate.text: How many queue callers hung up before an agent answered.

missed.text: Your calls today that did not connect.

sla.text: How often answered queue calls were picked up within the queue’s SLA threshold.

fcr.formula: callers with no repeat contact ÷ answered callers
fcr.text: Callers whose first answered queue call settled it: no repeat contact within the FCR window — no further queue call from them, answered or not, and no call back from us within the callback window. Numbers compare on their last nine digits; anonymous and internal callers are not counted.

avgWait.text: How long queue callers wait before someone picks up.

talkTime.text: Total time outbound calls spent with a customer on the line, wrap-up excluded.

callStatusTip.ANSWERED: Someone picked up and the two sides talked.
callStatusTip.UNANSWERED: It rang until it timed out, or our side gave up while it rang.
callStatusTip.BUSY: The callee was busy or declined the call.
callStatusTip.MISSED: The caller hung up while it was still ringing.
callStatusTip.UNREACHABLE: The phone was switched off, unregistered or out of service.
callStatusTip.FAILURE: The call could not be placed, for example a wrong number.
callStatusTip.NETWORK_ERROR: The route or the carrier failed: congestion or no circuit.
callStatusTip.ABANDONED: The caller hung up while waiting in a queue.
callStatusTip.DROPPED: The call was answered, then cut off abnormally.
